newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end firm, off contract high, spread narrows.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end firm, off contract high, spread narrows.

text.p: 1620 GMT - UK gilt futures ended firmer but below the new contract high reached after an unexpected drop in December UK retail sales. Data seen as increasing likelihood official rates will stay unchanged until after the election.
* March long gilt contract ended 24/32 higher at 111-20/32
"It appears that overall consumer demand is not as strong as a lot of the forecasts, including the Treasury's own forecast, for this year would suggest," said Tom Rayner, analyst at Societe Generale.
"We will need some significant pickup in activity if these 3.5 to four percent consumption forecasts for 1997 are to be met."
Most of the fall in retail sales was due to clothing, footwear and textiles, which were down 4.6 percent on the month.
"Stripping out this component, retail sales were flat in December," said Ciaran Barr of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"The negative tone of today's report supports the Chancellor's decision last week to keep rates on hold," he added.
"Unless next Monday's GDP report is very strong, the Chancellor may well decide to leave monetary policy unchanged at the February 5 monetary meeting."
Traders said the March gilt contract made several assaults on 111-28 during the session, drifting off in the early afternoon after Treasuries opened lower.
This is likely to be a key resistance level tomorrow if today's rally is sustained.
March short sterling ended seven basis points higher at 93.66, implying official interest rates of around 6.30 percent at the end of the first quarter.
The gilt-Bund spread at 10 years narrowed to 173 basis points from the previous 179.
